# Leadline

> Leadline is a local-first evidence router and policy engine for coding agents. It emits ordered evidence contracts, enforces routes through Claude Code hooks, grades bound tool-use receipts, traces decisions, and blocks unsupported completion claims.

Pronunciation: “LED-line.”
Tagline: Sound the source. Bring back proof.
License: MIT.
Status: pre-release; run from source. Claude Code is the only shipped host adapter.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): product overview, verified benchmark, source install, and current limitations
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): runtime loop, hook response semantics, state, locks, modes, and trust boundary
- [Policy packs](docs/policy-packs.md): YAML authoring contract, triggers, receipt rules, and structured-zero convention
- [Trace format](docs/trace-format.md): JSONL fields, verdicts, receipts, renderer, and storage
- [Exam protocol](docs/EXAM.md): frozen claim-detector exam methodology and provenance controls
- [Agent guide](AGENTS.md): repository map, commands, invariants, and change discipline

## Verified commands

```bash
npm install
npm test
npm run bench
node ./bin/leadline.js init --claude-code --dry-run
node ./bin/leadline.js trace --session <id>
```

## Current boundaries

- No npm publication yet; `npx leadline` is not a current install path.
- Claude Code has full enforcement. Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, and generic MCP-client adapters are roadmap work.
- Project-local policy packs are supported; per-project route and tell configuration is not.
- The hook loop has no LLM/network/telemetry path. Historical detector/evaluation tooling exists elsewhere in the repository and is not loaded by hooks.
